rounds.text: Mehai Technology Ltd trades at an extremely compelling valuation, including a price-to-book ratio of 0.39x compared to a sector benchmark of 5.75x [E2, E7] and a P/E multiple of 11.7x against a sector benchmark of 33.24x [E1, E6]. This discount stands in stark contrast to the company's phenomenal long-term compounding, featuring a 5-year profit growth CAGR of 141% and 3-year profit growth of 145% [E19, E20]. Fundamentals have dramatically outpaced share price performance, creating a scenario where a 5-year profit growth of 141% compares against a share price return of -17% [E22, E53]. Furthermore, operations are robustly cash-backed, with operating cash flow reaching Rs 12 Cr in March 2026, representing 114% of operating profit and a 1.71x cash conversion rate [E33, E34, E36]. The business also benefits from a supportive macroeconomic backdrop, with the Services sector operating in a verified tailwind [E74, E76]. Conceded: promoter holding has decreased by 15.71 percentage points since September 2023 down to 36.45%, free cash flow stands at Rs -31 Cr, and the share price rests at its 52-week low with a 0 relative-strength rating [E35, E40, E45, E48].

conceded: [E14] Despite reported historical growth metrics, Mehai Technology Ltd is suffering from severe operational decay, evidenced by trailing twelve-month sales growth slowing to just 2% [E17] and quarterly operating margins showing a consistent decrease over the last four quarters [E32]. The company exhibits chronic low profitability, with an ROE stuck at 4.6% to 5.86% [E13, E62] and a 10-year median ROE of only 5% [E25], heavily underperforming sector benchmarks [E9, E10]. Financial stress is further compounded by a massive free cash flow burn of negative Rs 31 Cr [E35], surging borrowings jumping from Rs 23 Cr to Rs 53 Cr in a single year [E38], and deteriorating working capital as debtor days stretch from 88.4 to 113 days [E64]. Compounding these fundamental red flags, insiders are rapidly exiting, with promoter holdings dropping significantly by 15.7 percentage points down to 36.45% [E40, E65], accompanied by a negative dividend yield of 0.00% [E4]. Market sentiment reflects this deep rot: the stock is sitting at the absolute bottom of its 52-week range (0% of range, down 93.6% from its high), trading below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages with a relative strength rating of zero [E5, E46, E47, E48].
